description: Optional host-native Jira tracker adapter layered on the run-delivery profile, whose commands run on POSIX hosts only. The adapter maps the neutral tracker operations onto the host's Atlassian MCP connector, configured by the repository's tracker properties, and the decomposition and tracked-execution workflows reach Jira only through it, without changing core behavior when tracking is unavailable. Delivery records can hold lane ownership, current story assignments, and temporary flakes scoped to a base commit and check. Authorized base merges can retain an aligned review through hand-off. Integration-base setup records its target and uses the integration checkout for delivery. Record writers are pinned by applied archive digest and changed through a parked lead transition. Integration-base moves preserve recorded commit ancestry and recover publication and applied-writer reconciliation once. A stopped base rerun is told from a failed one, a named repair lands first and alone through a queue its broken base stopped, and a finish line that covers nothing is the lead's to mark. Follow-ups are filed only for findings still deferred, a round card says when an approval carried deferrable notes, and a delivery may declare that it defers nothing. A base move that changed nothing a check reads, by the binding's own declaration, carries that check, and deliveries that merge into one base on a machine share one merge slot. The line map labels a carried check, a flaky base run and a peer's merge. A failed full-health run whose failing tests pass alone is recorded as flaky where the binding declares the rerun, lead-suite runs the lead's suite in its own checkout of a commit, and deliveries on one base see each other and warn on files a peer claimed. A bounded data-only public snapshot reuses line-map payloads while excluding history, raw artifacts and local execution details. Optional owned hosted publishing collects coherent source cuts, reconciles fenced writer receipts and keeps credentials out of view data and children. Owned hosted publishing starts or adopts an independent generation-aware watcher, bounds terminal close publication to 30 seconds, retains pending terminal cuts for ten-minute retries and supports credential-free archive viewing with explicit archive retry. Path-bearing public prose carries a visible omission marker while raw uploaded paths and configured secrets remain invalid. Credential-free terminal notifications reach an existing owner independently of lifecycle-lock contention and preserve one deadline per finished cut. Hosted publishing is qualified from exact built archive bytes in two independently configured adopters; the separately deployed viewer and its dependencies are excluded from workflow archives. Hosted diagnostics report configured hosting before a delivery is selected without reading or creating delivery state; missing credentials and malformed configuration remain explicit. Option-assigned local references and installed executable paths are omitted visibly from public prose and refused in raw uploads. Markdown, quote, bracket and diagnostic delimiters retain local-reference exclusion. ASCII punctuation includes Markdown emphasis; HTTPS URL components remain public prose. Closed URL wrappers leave adjoining local prose subject to exclusion while balanced URL punctuation survives. No-change settlement evidence uses public prose omission without changing private evidence or settlement identity. Workflows may consult an optional, read-only knowledge library after the repository's own solution notes; the hive knowledge adapter maps it to the host's hive-mined server, configured by the repository's knowledge properties, and a workflow reports that the library was not consulted when none is configured.
